summary: Every graded rule (2080 gain and halving, sub-noise exclusion, hypocentral distance, linear in-table interpolation, log-distance end-segment extrapolation off the table, additive correction, pooled per-station mean over both sensors' readings, median of stations counted once, null below three, report layout and order) is defined by NPM-4 or by the instruction's explicit keep-the-present-calculation rule. Hand traces of sampled expected values agree with that contract, so this review found no hidden convention, contradiction or representation-specific grading.
checks_performed: Reconciled all 38 manifest files with the files read; every expected .jsonl was read in full (single-line rows; limits.jsonl is one row).

Mapped each verifier comparison (tests/test_outputs.py:155-172) to NPM-4 section 6 and instruction.md:5: exact id, code, contributes, list order and null ml; numeric within 1e-6 (+1e-9 slack, more lenient than stated).

Mapped the load-time section-1 checks (tests/test_outputs.py:66-94) to NPM-4 1.1-1.3: 1 km minimum, 1 m margin at 10/600 km, one-part-in-a-thousand margin at 3x noise, <=2 recordings per station, >=1 reading per recording.
Hand-traced readings.jsonl line-1 LNA: 1.51 nm kept, 1.49 nm dropped (<1.5), ml=log10(1.51*1.04e-3)+3.0=0.19601; matches 0.196010287.
Hand-traced interpolation.jsonl K0 at 127 km: linear 3.0+0.3*27/50=3.162, plus log10(3037.1*1.04e-3)=0.49951, giving 3.66151; matches 3.661492431.

Hand-traced off_table.jsonl OFFA at 1000 km: log-distance extrapolation of the 500-600 segment gives -logA0=5.5745, ml=3.5915; matches 3.591532864 (linear extrapolation would give 5.91). OFFB at 5 km hypocentral with +0.1 correction gives 1.4570; matches 1.457033339. This confirms that the expectations use the instruction's keep-the-present-calculation rule, fed with hypocentral distance, the 2080 gain and halving, and the additive correction.

Hand-traced shared_station.jsonl shared-null SITA: pooled mean of (3.0170, 3.0170, 1.0170)=2.35037; matches 2.350366673 (a mean of recording means would give 2.017). Event is null with 2 distinct stations and 3 recordings, consistent with NPM-4 5.2/5.3 counting stations.
Checked half.jsonl HALF at 100 km: log10(1000*1040e-6)+3.0=3.017033; matches.

Checked that station_mean.jsonl chan-2 uses arbitrary channel codes ('?!.', 'xx9', 'Z Z', 'HHZ') and that instruction.md:5 ('any three-character channel codes') plus the no-exclusion clause (instruction.md:3) forbid channel-code filtering.
Checked that the driver identity requirement (instruction.md:1) matches tests/shipped/tools/ml_bulletin.py, which has the same hash as environment/app/tools/ml_bulletin.py in the manifest.
Checked that the runtime invocation (python3 -I -S, unprivileged, no network) creates no undisclosed interface obligation reachable by a stdlib implementation of the documented package.

coverage_sweep.category: Every grading rule traces to a sentence or authoritative candidate-visible artifact
coverage_sweep.reason: Magnification and halving (NPM 2.2), reading threshold (2.3), hypocentral distance (3.1), table and linear interpolation (3.2-3.3), additive correction (4.1-4.2), station mean over readings (4.3), contributor range (5.1), median and even-count rule (5.2), minimum of three (5.3) and report shape (6.1-6.2) are all stated. The off-table correction is governed by instruction.md:3 ('keep the present calculation ... fed with the quantities NPM-4 does define'), together with NPM 3.2 saying the manual gives no correction there and the shipped attenuation.py showing that calculation.

coverage_sweep.category: Permitted input domain and needed boundaries
coverage_sweep.reason: Section 1 gives the domain, including margins that remove the float-boundary ambiguities at 3x noise and at 10/600 km. The verifier enforces the same domain on every bulletin at load time. Instruction.md:3 leaves out-of-domain inputs open, and no graded bulletin falls outside the domain.

coverage_sweep.category: Rendered instruction, declared artifacts and verifier output paths agree
coverage_sweep.reason: The instruction names the command 'python3 /app/tools/ml_bulletin.py BULLETIN.json' on stdout and the /app/mlnet package. The verifier runs exactly that driver with a bulletin path and parses stdout. task.toml artifacts are /app/. The instruction contains no broken template text or sentinels.
The sample bulletin conforms to section 1. The README describes the package, driver and manual consistently. No worked example contradicts NPM-4.

Numbers are compared numerically, and bool, int and float types follow the JSON the driver emits. Key sets match NPM 6.1-6.2. Order requirements (file order, recording order) are stated in NPM 6.1. Tie-breaks do not arise, because the median uses values only.

Keeping the driver byte-identical is achievable, because the fix lives in /app/mlnet. The instruction's statement that NPM-4 governs (instruction.md:1) is consistent with NPM-4's own statement that it governs (npm4:6-7). The instruction's no-guard clause does not conflict with any NPM rule.

Each test targets a rule the contract states. The one rule the manual does not cover, off-table extrapolation, is explicitly assigned by the instruction to the present calculation, and the expected values match that assignment. The tolerance is at least as lenient as the one stated.
